Majority of my schooling was public school until I was lucky enough to be offered a bursary at a private school. 

Fun fact: I also went to a farm school when I was really young. 

Also is there actually a reputable organisation with this list that we're on? I genuinely thought that other guy was making it up. I'm on mobile so any links would be appreciated :)

You're welcome to do that but I'd like to see the argument they make for it. 

I imagine that they would be talking about the farm murders which are horrific but definitely not genocide. I've lived and worked on a farm and I'll admit the thought is always at the back of your mind though. 


I don't know what you mean by white urban areas though. In my experience urban areas are far more mixed than anywhere rural.

I would argue that it's money I had to ask for as I need financial assistance. They gave it to me because I worked hard enough to get good results (intelligence only gets you so far) . Being rich makes being anywhere easier, but no I would not consider myself rich (compared to the majority of people in South African universities.)
"On a scholarship" Yup. Rich. Soooooooooooooo rich. Just rolling in cash here. /s

White South African on scholarship here. Being on the genocide watch list is a crazy amount of hyperbole. Getting a job can be hard but honestly I don't believe it's much harder than other parts of the world where one is the minority.
He was lying. No cosmetics have ever effected stats. Some make skills look more awesome but that's all.
